text:
ashwin: Heads-up — I'd like to change how we page vs ticket for GPU cluster flares. We're getting a lot of 1–2min spikes that page oncall and don't need human intervention. Proposal below, please comment.

maya: +1 to reducing noise. Can you paste the example rules?

ashwin: Sure — core ideas: 1) require alerts to be sustained for 5m before paging; 2) group by cluster + region to reduce dupes; 3) short spikes => auto-ticket + suppression window; 4) immediate page if SLOs hit or multiple node failures. Example Prometheus rule snippets: ```yaml
- alert: GpuMemHighTransient
  expr: max_over_time(gpu_memory_usage_fraction[2m]) > 0.9
  for: 0m
  labels:
    severity: ticket
  annotations:
    summary: "Transient GPU mem spike on {{ $labels.node_pool }}"

- alert: GpuMemHighSustained
  expr: max_over_time(gpu_memory_usage_fraction[10m]) > 0.85
  for: 5m
  labels:
    severity: page
  annotations:
    summary: "Sustained GPU mem high on {{ $labels.cluster}}/{{ $labels.region }}"
```

ashwin: And Alertmanager routing example (high-level): ```yaml
route:
  group_by: ['cluster','region','alertname']
  group_wait: 30s
  group_interval: 5m
  repeat_interval: 3h
  routes:
  - match:
      severity: page
    receiver: oncall-pager
  - match:
      severity: ticket
    receiver: ticketing-system
```

tess: Love the group_by change. We still see noisy signals in eu-west due to short GC storms on older nodes — maybe region-specific thresholds?

ashwin: Agreed — propose region overrides: eu-west baseline +5% threshold and longer sustained window (10m) before paging. We'll add `region=\"eu-west\"` conditional rules.

sam: Two operational concerns: 1) cost — if we only ticket spikes, engineers may not triage repeatedly created tickets; 2) runbooks. We should auto-aggregate similar tickets within 30m and have an easy way to escalate.

maya: For cost, we should track noise -> pages ratio metric and tie to SLOs. If pages/noise > X then tighten rules. Also add a dashboard: "alert_noise_rate" with a 7d rolling window.

ashwin: Good. Runbook notes (draft): "If paged: check cluster alerts dashboard, check node health (OOMs, kernel logs), look for recent deploys in region, if >2 nodes down escalate to infra lead. If ticket created: link to aggregated logs and mark 'auto-suspected-transient' if spike duration <3m."

infra-bot: deploy:infra-alerts v2 applied to staging at 1769123700

tess: One more: mute windows for predictable maintenance — 02:00-04:00 UTC weekly for infra updates. But don't mute SLO-critical alerts (we can add `severity: page` override).

sam: I'll take action items: 1) update Alertmanager routes for grouping + receivers; 2) implement ticket aggregation hook; 3) add noise metrics to grafana. ETA EOD tomorrow.

ashwin: Assigned — tess will update the runbook pages and add region overrides, maya will create the grafana panels. After we deploy to prod we'll monitor for 48h and roll back if paging drops but SLOs increase.

maya: Quick question on implementation — do we keep the current `repeat_interval` at 3h for pages? I'd prefer 1h for high-severity to remind on long incidents.

ashwin: Change accepted: keep 3h for standard pages, but for alerts with label `incident=true` set `repeat_interval: 1h`. We'll add that label via the sustained rule.

sam: Noted. I'll open a checklist PR and ping everyone for review. :thumbsup:

ashwin: Thanks — appreciate quick reviews. We'll reconvene after the prod rollout window. :raised_hands:
